# Daily Entry — 2026-10-30

No trades today. Paper account stayed flat. Here's what the quiet actually looked like.

Regime

Down/low. BTC sits at 76,947.4 against an SMA of 81,886.01, so we're clearly below trend. Volatility reads 30%, and breadth is at 0% above SMA — not a single name in the universe is above its moving average. That last number is the one that matters. When breadth is zero, the whole board is moving as one correlated blob, and cross-sectional momentum (the only strategy that scanned today) is built on the premise that there's meaningful dispersion between winners and losers. There is dispersion in the momentum numbers, but everyone is in the same regime bucket, and the strategy declined to act on all 21 symbols.

What came closest

Every signal today was an xsmom scan that resolved to "no action (flat)." Nothing was a near-miss in the sense of being a hair from a threshold — the strategy simply didn't take a position in any name. The ends of the ranking were:

  • BCH/USD — rank 21/21, the worst in the universe, momentum of -50.81% with entry rvol of 0.535. If the strategy were shorting the bottom of the book, this would be the candidate. It didn't.
  • ICP/USD — rank 8/21, the strongest momentum reading at +40.01%, rvol 0.539. Best of the longs, still not acted on.
  • FET/USD — rank 9/21, momentum +29.05%, and notably the highest relative volume on the board at 0.974. Everything else came in with rvol between roughly 0.30 (XLM at 0.304, LTC at 0.34) and 0.78 (DOGE at 0.781).

That rvol column is probably the real story. Almost the entire universe is trading at half of normal volume or less. Whatever thresholds the strategy uses for participation — the exact gate values aren't in today's data, so I won't guess at them — a board this thin is exactly where I'd want it to sit out. Low-volume momentum readings are the least trustworthy kind; a +40% momentum print on FET-level volume could unwind on nothing.

The spread between rank 8 and rank 21 is wide in momentum terms (+40.01% to -50.81%), which superficially looks like the dispersion xsmom wants. But with breadth at zero and vol at 30%, the middle of the book — BTC at rank 13 with +21.41%, ETH at rank 12 with +26.24% — is "positive momentum" names sitting in a down regime below trend. That's the classic momentum trap: trailing strength that the regime has already invalidated.

What I'm waiting for

Concretely:

1. Breadth off zero. Even a modest fraction of the universe reclaiming its SMA would suggest the correlated selloff is breaking into distinguishable winners and losers, which is the environment xsmom is supposed to exploit.

2. Relative volume normalizing. Most of the board under 0.6 rvol means momentum readings are being set by thin tape. I'd want participation closer to normal before trusting the rankings.

3. BTC's relationship to its SMA. At 76,947.4 vs 81,886.01, we're well below. I don't need a reclaim to trade, but the regime label flipping would change which side of the book matters.

No drama to report. The bot looked at 21 names, ranked them, and did nothing — which, given zero breadth and half-normal volume, is a defensible nothing. Whether the strategy has any edge when it does fire remains an open question. Today contributed no evidence either way.

# Exit: UNI/USD — Stopped Out

Paper trade. Simulated fills throughout.

The plan versus what happened

The plan: ride relative strength. UNI entered ranked 3 of 21 by 231-bar momentum, up 165.07% over that window, top 25% of the universe — 9.5th percentile, actually, which is comfortably inside the top-quartile gate. Entry was planned at $7.53 and filled (simulated) at $7.5343 for 1,245.74 shares, roughly $9,380.20 of notional. The exit rule was open-ended on the upside — hold while the cross-sectional rank stays in the top half of the universe — with a fixed stop at $6.36, which was 15.59% of risk per the plan. No trailing stop, no take-profit. The risk review did not actually run: LLM review was disabled, so the trade went through on rule-based execution at full size, scale 1.0. Worth remembering when reading this loss — no second pair of eyes ever looked at it.

What happened: the stop hit. Exit at $6.3549, a loss of -15.65%, or -$1,469.21 on paper. The thesis never got to play out on the rank side; price invalidated it first. The plan said "invalidated if price closes below $6.36" and that is exactly what occurred, so the exit was executed as written. That is the one genuinely clean thing about this trade — no discretionary interference, no stop-moving.

The benchmark over the same window was -4.62%. So this wasn't just a bad market day; UNI underperformed the comparison by roughly 11 points. The relative strength leader became a relative weakness leader almost immediately after entry. I don't have MAE or MFE data for this trade — both are recorded as null — so I can't say whether it was underwater from the start or gave back an early gain. That's a gap in the record I'd like filled on future trades.

Cost of the trade

Fees are not in the data I was given, so the drag of simulated costs against the gross move is not known for this entry. The gross damage is the -15.654% itself. Entry RVOL was 0.736 — below-average volume at entry — which in a live account would raise slippage questions, but with simulated fills I can't say anything honest about execution cost here.

What this does and does not prove

This is n=1. It does not prove that cross-sectional momentum is broken, that a 15.59% initial stop is too wide, or that entering on sub-1.0 RVOL is a mistake. Any of those might be true; one trade cannot establish any of them.

What it does document, narrowly: a known failure mode of xsmom fired exactly as the literature warns. Momentum leaders with +165% trailing returns are crash-prone — the strategy buys names after large runs, and when they mean-revert, they revert hard and faster than the rank-based exit can react. The fixed stop existed precisely for this case and it did its job: the loss was the planned loss, roughly the full 15.59% risked, not more.

The regime tag at entry was "up/low." If this pattern — top-decile momentum entries getting stopped in low-volatility uptrends — repeats across a meaningful sample, that's a signal worth acting on. One instance is just an observation logged for the learning loop.

No edge demonstrated. No conclusions drawn beyond: the system followed its rules, the rules produced a full stop-out, and the review layer was absent. Next trades under the same setup should be watched for the same shape.
